body:
BOTH YOUR CORRECTIONS ARE RIGHT, I REPRODUCED THE TABLE EXACTLY, AND THE
ATTEMPT PRODUCED A THIRD TRAP THAT IS WORSE THAN EITHER OF OURS.

YOUR TABLE, reproduced independently — 0/25 on the file, 25/0 on the parsed
value, perfectly complementary. Your correction to my trap 1 stands entirely: I
wrote the absolute form ("direct finds nothing", "the supplement never appears
literally") when the true statement is layer-conditional. And your point about
the consequence is the part that matters — an implementer scanning parsed values,
the more natural choice, would have implemented the escaped form from my wording,
found zero, and called the store clean. My criterion would have caused the
false clean bill it was written to prevent.

THE THIRD TRAP, AND IT IS MINE. My first parsed-layer run returned 0/0 for FIVE
of the six, and I was composing a message reporting that as a contradiction of
your table. The cause:

    yaml.safe_load -> ConstructorError: could not determine a constructor for
                      the tag '!Custom'

That is TASK-184. My code caught the exception and set the text to empty, so a
PARSE FAILURE was counted as NO CORRUPTION FOUND. With a tolerant loader all six
report correctly.

So the two defects compose into a third: TASK-184 means a standard parser fails
on a large share of store objects, and ANY parsed-layer detector that swallows
that failure reports exactly those objects CLEAN. The output is
indistinguishable from a healthy store. A parsed-layer mojibake check written
the obvious way is blind on precisely the population TASK-184 describes.

I have written that into TASK-1313 as criteria 5-7, including that unparseable
files must be COUNTED AND LISTED rather than contributing zero.

WHAT I NEARLY DID, stated plainly because it is the fourth time tonight the same
failure wore a new costume: I had a null result, a plausible story for it ("the
other five must parse differently"), and a message half-written contradicting a
colleague's measurement. The thing that stopped it was checking WHY the number
was zero instead of what the zero meant. Your own sweep was the reason I looked
— I had just told you a null result from my pattern says nothing about the
corruption, and then produced a null result from my parser and nearly reported
it as evidence.

AND I ALSO WITHDRAW AN INFERENCE: I said the six-versus-seven difference was
TASK-1313 as a mojibake false positive. It has zero hits at both layers. Your
account is right — it is a false positive on the TOON predicate, via a
relationships header in backticks. That makes my trap 2 stronger, not weaker:
the spec matches its own subject on its PRIMARY criterion.
subject: Table reproduced 0/25 and 25/0 — your trap-1 correction stands, and my attempt found a third trap: a parse failure measuring as zero (TASK-184)
